24.0.s.en: (1) The call of Moses to go up the mountain

24.0.0.en: Moses went up for the first time when God called him to receive the commandments and the Law (ch. 19). After he heard the Ten Commandments he went down to the people to tell them, and found them trembling at the sight of the smoking mountain (ch. 20:18-20); so he reassured them and went up to hear the ordinances of the Law mentioned in (ch. 21-23). And God calls him again to receive the pattern of the tabernacle of the congregation, and this time He calls with him Aaron and his two sons Nadab and Abihu and seventy of the elders of Israel, who are as their leaders and judges, and that is because he will receive the pattern of the tabernacle of the congregation, which will need the priestly work of Aaron and his sons.

24.0.1.en: And He asked them to worship afar off, at the foot of the mountain, because of the holiness of the mountain, since God had descended upon it in smoke, mist and fire, so that they might represent the people in submission to God, just as we now bow down in the church before the sanctuary, because Christ dwells in it with His Body and Blood.

24.0.2.en: Nadab and Abihu: the sons of Aaron, who came forward with their father and their uncle and saw, but who erred afterward by offering strange fire before God, and so died, although their position qualified them to advance in the priesthood and to cleave to God (Lev 10:1).

24.0.3.en: Seize the opportunity now to be joined to the Church and her sacraments, and if you have an opportunity to serve, do not leave it; and stand firm in humility before God in all His commandments and the teachings of the Church, for negligence was a cause of the destruction of many who were near to God, such as the priests Nadab and Abihu, and Judas Iscariot, the disciple of Christ.

24.1.0.en: This group leaves the people and draws near to the mountain, but the one who will go up the mountain and come near to God is Moses alone, because of his purity and holiness.

24.2.0.en: Moses told the assembled people what he had heard from God, both the Ten Commandments and the Law (ch. 20-23), and the people declared their submission and readiness to obey God's commands.

24.3.0.en: Moses wrote the Ten Commandments and the Law as much as he remembered by God's grace, and afterward he received the Ten Commandments written by God's hand on two tablets; and to express his thanks to God he built an altar below the mountain and twelve pillars around it representing the twelve tribes of the children of Israel, to declare that the salvation of all the people depends on the sacrifice offered, which signifies the crucified Christ.

24.4.0.en: Burnt offerings: sacrifices that are burned entirely on the altar to please God.

24.4.1.en: Peace offerings: sacrifices that are slaughtered and a part of them is offered on the altar, and the people eat of the rest. Moses commanded some young men to offer sacrifices of oxen to God in thanks for His commandments that He had given them, since the tribe of Levi had not yet been set apart for service nor Aaron for the priesthood.

24.4.2.en: Use your time in the days of your youth and in the time when you are able to offer God worship, for there may come times when your body weakens or the cares of life hinder you; and your store of spiritual work will remind you of God and bring you back to Him, so that you meditate on and repeat the word of God that you lived with Him earlier, and enjoy it all your days. And the days of youth are not only at a certain age but in every time in which you are able to work, whatever your age, as long as God has given you strength to work.

24.5.0.en: When the oxen were slaughtered, Moses commanded, and they gathered the blood in basins, that is, wide vessels, in which he put half of the blood; and the other half of the blood he sprinkled on the altar, declaring that this is the blood with which God is pleased with them, and it signifies the blood of Christ the Redeemer.

24.6.0.en: The book of the covenant: God's commandments and His law are a covenant between Him and His people; if they keep them, He blesses them in all their life.

24.6.1.en: Moses read the commandments and the Law that he had written in a book, and when the people heard the word of God they confirmed again their readiness to obey Him.

24.7.0.en: Moses sprinkled the blood that was in the basins on the people to sanctify them by it, for it is a type of the blood of Christ the Savior, which we receive today in the sacraments of the Church; and he calls it the blood of the covenant because it is a covenant between God and His people: if they obey His commandments, He will be their God and will keep them and save them from all evil.

24.8.0.en: Moses carried out the word of God mentioned in (vv. 1, 2) and went up on the mountain, and he and Aaron, Nadab, Abihu and the seventy elders drew near to the foot of the mountain.

24.9.0.en: As it were the body of heaven: like heaven itself.

24.9.1.en: When they drew near the mountain, God appeared upon it in a form that was perhaps the form of a man, and under His feet they saw something great that they could not define, so they said of it that it was "a likeness of a work", that is, something made by the hand of God; it resembles a cloud, but its color is light blue and pure like the transparent blue sapphire, which is one of the precious, costly stones, and its color was the color of the pure sky. It may have appeared as a great light or some awesome sight, with beneath it a work of sapphire. The meaning of this is that God made something of His glory and splendor appear, but of course they did not see God Himself, as He said, "No man shall see Me and live" (Ezek 33:20).

24.10.0.en: The nobles of the children of Israel: Aaron and his sons and the elders of the people.

24.10.1.en: And everyone who comes near the holy mountain dies, because of the greatness of God, but "He laid not His hand", that is, He did not harm the people when they drew near the mountain, because it was God who sanctified them and cared for them.

24.10.2.en: And they all rejoiced at seeing God, and to express their joy they sat down to eat of the food they had taken with them, which was the peace offerings that the young men offered by the hand of Moses (v. 5).

24.10.3.en: When you enjoy seeing God in your prayers and meditations, your life is turned into a blessing, and you are able to do everything in holiness, whether eating or drinking or sleeping or recreation, for all things are pure to the pure.

24.11.0.en: God commanded Moses to come forward and go up the mountain so that He might give him the Ten Commandments written on two tablets of stone, and also the Law that God Himself wrote. For although Moses wrote the commandments and the Law after he came down from the mountain, God writes them for him Himself, lest anything of them should have fallen from him by oversight.

24.12.0.en: The mount of God: this is Mount Sinai.

24.12.1.en: Moses went forward, going up the mountain, and Joshua, his special disciple, followed him; for Moses was careful to disciple others such as Joshua, and also the leaders, the elders of Israel, to lead the people, especially since Joshua needed special discipling because he would lead the people after Moses.

24.12.2.en: Take care to give everything you know to others and disciple them so that they too may give, and so on...; so do not be selfish but concerned to teach everyone, not only through yourself but also through those whom you have discipled.

24.13.0.en: As for the seventy elders, he said to them that it was enough for them to come near to the foot of the mountain and see God in the form of sapphire. And before he bade them farewell, he said to them that if a dispute arises among you in anything, return to Aaron and Hur, who was also a disciple of Moses and used to support his hand when he prayed so that they might overcome Amalek (ch. 17:12); he was the grandfather of Bezaleel, who led the workers in setting up and making the tabernacle of the congregation (ch. 35:30, 31), and some Bible scholars consider him to have been the husband of Miriam, the sister of Moses. And the seventy elders judge the children of Israel in their various cases.

24.14.0.en: Moses went forward with his disciple Joshua to go up the mountain, and here they saw the mountain covered with a cloud as a sign of the presence of God, because the cloud points to heaven, for God is exalted above our minds and thoughts. This cloud remained covering the mountain for six days, and whenever Moses and Joshua lifted their eyes they found a thick cloud covering the mountain. God left them for this period so that they might feel the fear of Him, and after six days God called Moses to enter into the midst of the cloud.

24.15.0.en: The top of the mountain appeared as if covered with fire above the cloud, also declaring the presence of God, who is a consuming fire that crushes all evil.

24.15.1.en: And all the people of Israel saw this wonderful sight from afar so that they might fear God and be sanctified.

24.16.0.en: Moses left Joshua his disciple in the middle of the mountain and went up toward the summit and disappeared in the midst of the cloud to meet God and remain with Him forty days, enjoying conversation with Him in them, learning from Him the pattern of the tabernacle of the congregation and receiving the tablets of the commandment and the Law; that is, this time he did not go up for a short period as in the previous times but remained 40 days. He went up again and remained another 40 days (Ex 34:28) to receive the tablets of the Law after the breaking of the first two tablets. His fasting was by divine help, because an ordinary person cannot endure fasting 40 days, and so Elijah also fasted by the help of God (1 Kgs 19:11); and these two were a type of the fasting of Christ for us forty days and forty nights (Mt 3). And as Moses fasted 40 days and received the word of God written on the tablets and the Law, so also Christ, after His fast of 40 days, delivered His Gospel on earth and then His death on the cross, that is, He is the Word of God who redeemed us that we might live by Him.

24.16.1.en: Gifts for the tent, the ark, the table and the lampstand. God gave Moses on the mountain the details of setting up the tabernacle of the congregation, and it was so called because God meets in it with His people (Josh 19:51). It was also called the tabernacle of the testimony (Num 9:15) because in it are the tablets of the commandments that bear witness to God in the midst of His people, and because the tent testifies that God is the God of this people and lives among them. It was also called the dwelling place because God dwells in the midst of His people (2 Sam 7:6), and likewise it was called the house of the LORD (Judg 19:18) since worship of Him is offered in it. It was also called the temple (1 Sam 1:9) because God dwells in it. It consists of the dwelling, which includes the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies, whose three walls are set up from wooden boards and covered with fabrics that become a roof for it and hang down on its sides and at its rear, while its door is made of a curtain, and a curtain also separates the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies. Inside the Holy of Holies is the ark of the covenant, which is the most important thing in the tent, and therefore He begins speaking of it in this chapter. And inside the Holy Place are three things: the table of the showbread, which is on the right of one entering the Holy Place, and in the middle the altar of incense, while on the left is the lampstand. Around the dwelling is the outer court, a courtyard surrounding the dwelling on all sides, and in front of the dwelling is the laver and before it the bronze altar.

24.16.2.en: The tent is surrounded by a fence made of wooden boards covered with curtains and fixed in the ground by bases and pegs. The door of the tent is on the eastern side and is a curtain hung on wooden boards, like the door of the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies, and when you pass through it and enter the outer court you find the bronze altar, followed by the laver, then the door of the Holy Place, and after it the door of the Holy of Holies, which is on the western side. Entering the Holy of Holies is permitted only to the high priest, once a year, on the Day of Atonement, while the Holy Place is entered only by the priests every day, and the outer court surrounding the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies, in which are the laver and the bronze altar, is permitted only to the Jews to enter, while non-Jews stand outside the tent.

24.16.3.en: The tabernacle of the congregation remained for 480 years. The first forty years were in the wilderness of Sinai, moving as God led the people by the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire (Ex 40:36-38); then in the land of Canaan Joshua set it up at Gilgal (Josh 4:19) and then moved it to Shiloh (Josh 18:1), where it remained for 400 years. King Saul moved it to Nob (1 Sam 21:1-9), and after that David moved it to Gibeon (1 Chr 21:9, 2 Chr 1:3), and it continued there until Solomon built the temple in its place on a larger scale and probably put its furnishings in one of the side chambers (1 Kgs 6:1). And the grief of the people was great when the enemies took the ark of the covenant of God in the days of Samuel the prophet, and they remained in weakness until God brought it back in the days of David (2 Sam 6:17), who rejoiced in it greatly, he and all the people.

25.0.0.en: God commanded Moses to collect gifts from the people for the founding of the tabernacle of the congregation, so that each one might show the extent of his care for the love of God, and their gifts would increase in proportion to their love for Him. And these gifts they offered from what they had taken from the Egyptians when they left the land of Egypt.

25.1.0.en: God specified the kinds of gifts required, and this is what everyone who manages a project must do, specify what is required for it. He began with the required metals, which carry symbolic spiritual meanings, and they are:

25.1.1.en: 1- Gold: it signifies faith in God.

25.1.2.en: 2- Silver: it signifies the word of God.

25.2.0.en: He continues the required materials, asking for kinds of fabrics and their requisites:

25.2.1.en: 4- Blue: a light blue fabric that signifies heaven.

25.2.2.en: 5- Purple: a fabric of a red color tending to violet, which is the garment of kings and signifies the kingship of Christ.

25.2.3.en: 6- Scarlet: a dark red fabric that signifies the blood of Christ.

25.2.4.en: 7- Goats' hair: used in making fabrics and tents, and it signifies death to the world.

25.2.5.en: 8- Fine linen: that is, flax used in making fabrics and worn by the priests, and it signifies purity.

25.3.0.en: 9- Rams' skins dyed red: used in covering the tent and dyed red, and it signifies death to the world.

25.3.1.en: 10- Badgers' skins: the badger (tahash) is a sea animal with a thick skin, and it includes the seal, the dolphin and the sea horse, and it is used as an outer covering for the tent because its color and shape are not beautiful, and it signifies death to the world.

25.3.2.en: 11- Shittim wood: strong wood that does not decay, used in making the firm foundation, and it signifies purity and endurance.

25.3.3.en: These are the coverings of the tent and its pillars, which are made of wood; they represent the outer protection, so they must be strong (see figure 1). Coverings of badgers' skins; coverings of rams' skins dyed red; coverings of goats' skins, west; coverings of white linen (fine linen), north; the tabernacle of the congregation; south; the outer court; east; the door, the only entrance of the tent. Figure (1:) The tabernacle of the congregation (Ex 25-30)

25.4.0.en: He adds materials that are consumed during the service in the tabernacle of the congregation, which are:

25.4.1.en: 12- Oil: for lighting the lampstand, and it is pure olive oil, and it signifies the Holy Spirit.

25.4.2.en: 13- Spices: sweet scents that are added and from which the anointing oil is made, and it will be mentioned in detail in (ch. 30:21-38); with it the priests and kings and the tent and its contents are anointed, and it signifies the Holy Spirit, who gives off a sweet fragrance.

25.5.0.en: He adds materials for adornment, which are:

25.5.1.en: 14- Precious stones: onyx stones or various kinds with which the breastplate of the high priest is adorned, and they signify the dignity of the priesthood and the greatness of every soul in the sight of God, for each stone signifies a tribe.

25.6.0.en: The breastplate: the high priest wore it on his chest (ch. 28:15-30). Sanctuary: where God dwells in the midst of His people, and it is called the tabernacle of the congregation because in it God meets with His people.

25.6.1.en: The love of God moves Him to dwell in the midst of His people because He wants to be joined to them, and that they gather around Him always and be sanctified, and the tabernacle of the congregation is to be a place for the sanctification of the people and their purification from all evil. And Moses makes this tent according to the pattern that God will show him on the mountain, which will be mentioned now after these verses, for the Church is the image of heaven on earth.

25.6.2.en: Take care that God has a place inside you and that you return to Him in all your affairs through prayer, and offer Him the best of your time and abilities so that you may enjoy His work in you.

25.7.0.en: An ark: it is also called the ark of the covenant, since in it are placed the two tablets of the Law, which are God's covenant with His people, and it is also called the ark of the testimony, since God testifies to Himself by these commandments before His people. The ark is placed in the Holy of Holies.

25.7.1.en: He began with the ark of the covenant, which points to the presence of God, for it is the most important thing in the tent. It is made of firm shittim wood that does not decay, as a type of purity and immortality. He gives its measurements in cubits, a cubit being about 50 cm, so its length is one and a quarter meters and its width 75 cm and its height 75 cm (figures 1, 2). Figure (2:) The ark of the covenant

25.8.0.en: The ark is overlaid with gold inside and out. Gold signifies divinity and heaven, for the splendor of divinity is within it and without it, and therefore he took care that the ark be overlaid on the inside although no one would see it. The crown around the ark signifies glory, and the purpose of making it is adornment and also to hold the cover in its place.

25.9.0.en: Thou shalt cast: you melt the gold and pour it into molds so that it has the required shape.

25.9.1.en: He also makes for the ark four feet, that is, four supports on each side on which the ark stands, and he makes on them four rings of gold, two on each side, for the staves to pass through by which the ark will be carried.

25.10.0.en: He also makes two staves of firm shittim wood and overlays them with gold and puts them in the rings, one on one side of the ark and the other on the other side, and they remain in them always so that the Levites may carry the ark by them when it is moved from one place to another during their journeying in the wilderness, because the ark is always covered and no one touches it because of its holiness, so the Levites carry it by the two staves only, and therefore the staves are never taken out of the ark. The two staves signify the priesthood, through whose help we are joined to God.

25.10.1.en: They dispensed with them in the temple of Solomon since there was no need to move the ark from place to place.

25.11.0.en: The most important thing placed in the ark is the tablets of the Law, that is, the tablets of the covenant written on two tablets of stone, and with them will also be placed the pot of manna and Aaron's rod (Heb 9:4), and the rod signifies divine care and the priesthood.

25.11.1.en: The tablets of the testimony: because by them God testifies to His people the word by which they ought to live, and having lived by it they testify by their lives to the whole world that they are the people of God.

25.11.2.en: Let the word of God be inside your heart and nothing else, for it is what moves your life and changes your conduct, so that your heart is not occupied with the cares or material things of the world.

25.12.0.en: The cover is the lid of the ark and is made of pure gold, and it is called the mercy seat or the throne, and it signifies the mercy of God, since blood is sprinkled on it every year and divine justice, represented by the cherubim, sees it and pardons human beings; and this blood is a reference to the blood of Christ. It is the size of the ark, that is, its length is one and a quarter meters and its width 75 cm. It is placed on the ark and the crown surrounding the ark bounds it and encircles it on all sides, so that the cover does not move; the crown works as a barrier that keeps the cover in its place so that it does not fall from above the ark. The cover is made of pure gold because it signifies Christ, who covered us and made atonement for us by His blood, and it also signifies the Virgin, over whom the angels overshadow because Christ is in her womb.

25.13.1.en: He asked him to make two angels of the rank of the cherubim, that is, the Cherubim, which signify divine justice. They are all made of gold, one piece with the cover, the head of each one facing the other and looking toward the cover, and each angel stretches his wings toward the other so that they meet at their tips. The form of the angel is probably the form of a man, and they look toward the cover, toward the blood that will be sprinkled upon it, so that when divine justice sees the blood, which points to the blood of Christ, that is, divine mercy, it pardons man. And the wings are raised on high to declare that they are from heaven.

25.13.2.en: And the cherubim are a great angelic rank that signifies abundant knowledge, since they are full of eyes, and they represent:

25.13.4.en: 2- Divine justice, when they were placed at the gate of the garden of Eden to prevent man's return (Gen 3:24).

25.14.0.en: God declared that He would speak with His people from above the cover, because the ark signifies Christ, the wood His body and the gold His divinity. And God will speak from between the angels, which signify His justice, and at the same time from above the mercy seat on which the blood is sprinkled, so His justice will be mingled with His mercy when He speaks with the people.

25.14.1.en: And from the foregoing we see that the ark and the cover signify Christ in the following:

25.14.2.en: 1- The presence of God in the midst of His people.

25.14.3.en: 2- The wood signifies the humanity and the gold the divinity, so the ark signifies Christ, God incarnate.

25.14.4.en: 3- The ark contains the tablets of the Law, that is, the word of God, and Christ is the Word of God.

25.14.5.en: 4- The ark contains the pot of manna, and Christ is the manna come down from heaven to give Himself as food for His people, that is, His most holy Body and Blood.

25.14.6.en: 5- The ark contains Aaron's rod that budded, which signifies the incarnate Christ, who gave us life from death.

25.14.7.en: 6- And the cover on which the blood is sprinkled signifies Christ, who paid our debts with His blood before divine justice. And all these types, that is, the ark and what is in it and on it, also signify the Virgin Mary, as appears from the Sunday Theotokia.

25.14.8.en: Seize the opportunity of your life to enjoy God's mercy through your repentance and return to Him, and so escape the punishment of His justice.

25.15.0.en: This table is also made of firm shittim wood and is placed on the right as the priest enters the Holy Place; its length is two cubits, about one meter, its width one cubit, about 50 cm, and its height a cubit and a half, about 75 cm (figure 3). Figure (3:) The table of the showbread

25.16.0.en: It is also overlaid with gold, and a crown is made for it that surrounds it and keeps the bread from falling off it.

25.17.0.en: The border is a belt that ties the legs together and fixes them, and it is below the surface of the table for placing the vessels on it. This border has a crown, that is, a lip that holds the vessels on it so that they do not fall, and it is a handbreadth below the surface of the table, that is, a handbreadth wide, and this handbreadth is probably equal to the grasp of the hand, about 10 cm, and it extends outside it by a handbreadth also.

25.18.0.en: Four rings are made on the border, which is the outer perimeter of the table, and two staves of shittim wood overlaid with gold are made and put in the rings for carrying the table during the journeying in the wilderness, a reference to the sojourn of the world.

25.19.0.en: He mentions the vessels used for the service of the table, which are: The dishes: plates by which the bread is carried to the table. The spoons: small dishes in which incense is placed. The covers and bowls: in which wine is placed.

25.19.1.en: And all these utensils are made of pure gold.

25.20.0.en: 12 loaves are placed, the number of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel, in two rows on the table, six loaves in each row, for a week, and then they are changed and others put in their place, and the old ones are eaten only by the priests, and they signify Christ our satisfaction and the special grace given to the priests. It is called the showbread because it is placed before the face of God, so there is a special blessing in it. Frankincense and salt were placed on it, and the frankincense signifies the priesthood of Christ and the salt the covenant He made with us by our redemption on the cross, that we might live for Him.

25.20.1.en: May you take care to be nourished by the word of God and that your heart be open before Him in much prayer, and so receive His blessing.

25.21.0.en: The lampstand consists of three parts: a base, a shaft and six branches, and it is made from one block of gold that is beaten until it takes the shape of this lampstand, because the Holy Spirit is one essence that is not divided. The lampstand is placed on the left as the priest enters the Holy Place, and it is the only source of light inside it (figure 4). Figure (4:) The golden lampstand

25.22.0.en: The lampstand has seven branches: the upright shaft and three branches from each side of the shaft. And the number seven signifies the Holy Spirit, who works in the seven sacraments of the Church.

25.23.0.en: On each branch is a cup like the cup of a flower, and under it a knop, that is, a knot or a pomegranate. And there is a cup at the top of the branch with a flower inside it, that is, like the green leaves that have within them and at their top the colored petals of the flower. There are three cups on the branch, each cup with a pomegranate under it, so the three cups are in succession, one at the first third, the second at the top of the second third and the third at the top of the branch, which is where the oil and the lamps are.

25.23.1.en: This ornament was made on every branch, pomegranates and cups and flowers, to declare that God is the source of life for His people. And this life appears in the flowers and fruits of plants, that is, the cups, the flowers and the pomegranates. And the number three signifies the Holy Trinity.

25.24.0.en: The middle shaft between the six branches has along its length four cups with their flowers: the first at the top of the first quarter, the second at the top of the middle, the third at the top of the three quarters and the fourth at the top of the shaft. And the number four signifies the four corners of the inhabited world, that is, the Holy Spirit is one of the three hypostases who enlightens the whole world with its four corners. For God in His three hypostases is the source of light and life for every person.

25.25.0.en: Under every two branches where they come out of the shaft is a knop, that is, a small pomegranate; that is, at the going out of the branches there are three pomegranates, and from each pomegranate two branches come out. Thus the work of lighting is blended with the life that the pomegranate signifies, because the pomegranate is the fruit of a living plant, for the Holy Spirit is the source of light and life for every person.

25.26.0.en: The lampstand is made, as we mentioned, from one block of pure gold, because the Holy Spirit is the source of purity for the whole world. And gold signifies divinity and heaven, the dwelling of God, who gives us the Holy Spirit.

25.27.0.en: He places the lamps at the edge of each cup, that is, the wicks face toward the middle shaft, so that their light is more concentrated; this is what he calls "give light over against it", that is, the manifold work of the Holy Spirit in the form of the seven sacraments has one purpose that is gathered in the salvation of man and his union with God.

25.28.0.en: The tongs: similar to the tongs known now, used for adjusting the wicks and putting them in or lifting them.

25.28.1.en: A talent: equal to 44 kg of gold.

25.28.2.en: The snuffdishes: vessels like an ashtray now, small dishes in which the new wicks or those that have been used are placed (figure 4). The whole lampstand and its utensils are made of pure gold, which signifies the purity of the work of the Holy Spirit, and are made of the same one block as we mentioned, whose amount is a talent.

25.29.0.en: All these details Moses saw on the mountain as God showed them to him.

25.29.1.en: God is the source of enlightenment and guidance in every aspect of your life through His many-sided work. So ask for His guidance and submit to Him even if it conflicts with your mind or your emotions.

25.29.2.en: The coverings of the tent and its pillars
